price_per_million.source: copied from reasoning_models_v1 (confirmed 2026-11-11); thinking tokens billed as output

methodological_questions: How is 'role travels' operationalised for a mover, and is it the same measure for cut-heavy and drive-heavy shapers?
Can a between-group difference in portability be detected with n=24 units?
How are cut-heavy and drive-heavy defined from play-type possession records without using outcome-derived labels or the portability outcome?
How should regression to the mean, mover selection, destination-team context and play-type-rate confounding be handled?
Is the group contrast better run as a continuous moderator on the larger mover set than as two small groups?

historical_evidence.finding: Portability confirmatory T1: a mover's displacement signature is more similar across franchises than profile-matched destination decoys' signatures. Median Delta=+0.0557, perm p=0.0050, 173/294 positive (58.8%), sign p=2.87e-3, destination-franchise CI [+0.0192,+0.0859]. The record lists PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE as a risk.

Portability feasibility gate passed with 294 movers in the final output (296 in the prereg record). The vacuity rho was 0.007 in the final output against 0.048 in the prereg record. The record notes that the mover count and rho changed between prereg and final output.
Team offensive association structure is more similar to itself across split halves than to other teams, and this persists after residualizing play-type rates (residual R2=0.043).

Structural influence is not reducible to usage (F1a residual share about 0.90). The usage-residual is a reproducible player property (F1b pooled rho about +0.67). The record lists measurement reliability as a limitation.

Connector diet x destination gap match: taxonomy-connector subsets of n=5/14 (n=19 total) gave p=0.156. The all-movers binary p=0.0283 did not replicate as a continuous Spearman. Failure mechanism A_unanswerable, limited by small sample.

Structural load L(p) and an |dA|-weighted ecosystem lift did not predict teammate-path quality beyond a uniform average of teammate lifts (residual r=+0.084, p=0.399; n=102). Failure mechanism B_powered_null.
Apparent cross-possession play-type memory (including DRIVE and CUT lag effects) disappeared after team-season demeaning. The flat, non-decaying lifts were produced by team-quality confounding.

Persistent Impact Score Level 1 gate failed the decay sanity check: DRIVE lifts were flat, and within-team DRIVE lag-1 fell to about zero. The record's verdict is failed_gate and it cites a team-quality confound.
The player-routing gain shrank from +0.94 to +0.03 pts/100 on the larger 520-matchup sample. The record notes the outcomes were model-scored.
Short-memory horizon of about 2-3 possessions, stable out of sample (n=1,024,980 possessions, time-split test on 2025-26). Absolute AUC is only about 0.59.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Subgroup comparison among connector movers (matched vs mismatched), n=5/14 within n=19
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as A_unanswerable and limited by small sample. The all-movers binary effect did not replicate with a continuous measure.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Global play-type lift comparisons without within-team baselines
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as C_artifact: team-quality confounding, with lifts vanishing after team-season demeaning.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Play-type memory gate for DRIVE and other play types
failed_approaches.why: The flat lifts failed the decay sanity check under a within-team baseline (team-quality confound).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Scalar or weighted structural metrics used as predictors
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as B_powered_null: the metrics added nothing beyond a uniform average.

evidence_establishes: For the pooled set of about 294 movers, the displacement signature is somewhat more similar across franchises than for profile-matched decoys (FAM:SF19, supported). A portability estimand and a decoy-based comparison already exist in this project.
Earlier work found that small mover subsets (n=19) could not support subgroup contrasts (FAM:SF-APPS-090, untestable).
Earlier work found that raw play-type comparisons that ignore team context can produce artifacts, including for DRIVE (FAM:SF-APPS-073, FAM:SF-CHT-029).
Structural influence is reproducible and not reducible to usage (FAM:SF18).
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether portability differs by cut-heavy vs drive-heavy profile. No retrieved record compares these profiles.
How 'shaper' is defined, or how many of the roughly 294 movers are shapers.
Whether the n=24 units are movers, shapers or player-seasons, or whether they are independent.
Whether the T1 portability effect (median Delta about +0.056) is large enough to leave room for a detectable group difference.
own_inferences: With about 12 units per group and a small pooled effect, a two-group test has very low power. Only a very large standardised difference would be detectable.

Cut-heavy players are likely to have low usage and to depend on teammates (for example passers), while drive-heavy players create their own offence. Differences in portability could therefore reflect destination context or usage rather than role type.
A direction is plausible (cutters depend on teammates, so their roles could travel worse), so the stated direction may be wrong rather than merely unproven.

The stated hypothesis could be tested more powerfully as a continuous cut-share minus drive-share moderator of the portability Delta in the full mover set. That is a different test from the n=24 two-group contrast.
If the profile is defined from the same play-type records used to compute portability, profile and outcome are partly mechanically linked.
uncertainties: The definition of 'shaper' and of the profile thresholds is not in the task or the retrieved records. I did not consult the glossary.
Whether the n=24 units are a subset of the 294 movers.
The record FAM:SF-PAP-016 notes that the mover count and vacuity rho changed between prereg and final output, so the pipeline is not fully frozen.
The portability measure's reliability for low-volume players is unknown (see FAM:SF18's measurement-reliability limitation).

historical_effect.explanation: The earlier portability family (FAM:SF19) supplies a defined estimand and a decoy comparison, so the construct is measurable. The untestable result in FAM:SF-APPS-090 on n=19 and the artifact results in FAM:SF-APPS-073 and FAM:SF-CHT-029 show that the n=24 group contrast and raw play-type comparisons are likely to fail. This moved the decision from a naive proceed to do_not_proceed as posed, with a minimum viable test on the larger mover set.

blocking_constraints.text: n=24 split into two profile groups gives about 12 per group, which is too few to detect a difference in a small median portability effect.
Cut vs drive profile is confounded with usage, role, position and destination-team context.
Portability signatures for low-volume players are noisy, and cut-heavy players tend to have fewer touches.

prior_work.summary: Pooled portability of the displacement signature has been confirmed (FAM:SF19). The profile-specific contrast (cut-heavy vs drive-heavy) has not been tested in any retrieved record. Related small-subset contrasts were untestable (FAM:SF-APPS-090).

risks.text: There are about 12 units per group, and the pooled effect is small.
Usage, role, minutes, destination-team structure and team quality can drive both profile and portability. Earlier artifacts (FAM:SF-APPS-073) came from team-level confounds.

If the cut-heavy/drive-heavy label is derived from the same possession records that produce the portability signature, the label and outcome are mechanically related. Labels must come from pre-move data only.
Movers and shapers are selected, and extreme cut-share or drive-share values regress toward the mean after the move.
Low-volume cutters have noisy signatures, which attenuates or distorts the group difference.
Portability is defined relative to decoys (as in FAM:SF19), so the result depends on how well the decoys are matched.
Several thresholds, definitions and measures can be tried, which inflates false positives.
Seasons span 2022-23 to 2025-26, and the 2025-26 playoffs are only partial before 2026-06-21.

design.estimand: The difference in portability Delta (self-similarity minus profile-matched decoy similarity of the displacement signature) between cut-heavy and drive-heavy shapers. The primary form is the slope of Delta on a continuous pre-move (cut share minus drive share) profile score. The binary-group contrast is secondary.
design.unit: Mover-move (a player moving franchises), clustered by destination franchise and by player.
design.sample: Minimum viable test: all movers meeting the FAM:SF-PAP-016 gate (about 294 in earlier work), restricted to shapers by a definition fixed before analysis. Profile is computed only from pre-move possessions. The n=24 group contrast is exploratory only. If the shaper subset is below about 80 movers, report as untestable.
design.power: Set a minimum detectable effect before analysis. With n=12 per group, only about a 1.2 SD difference in Delta is detectable at 80% power and alpha=0.05, which is implausible given the pooled effect. Use a power gate: the moderator test needs at least about 80 shaper movers with a pre-move sample above a minimum number of possessions. Otherwise stop.
design.controls: Control for pre-move usage, minutes, position, destination team quality and destination structural gap. Use decoys matched on profile and usage, and use within-team (team-season demeaned) baselines, as in the artifact lessons of FAM:SF-APPS-073. Handle regression to the mean with split-half pre-move profile estimation. Require a minimum number of possessions on both sides of the move.
design.falsification: Run a placebo with shuffled profile labels, a placebo using non-movers split across seasons within the same franchise, and a negative-control moderator (for example, random profile score). If the profile effect disappears after usage adjustment, label it an artifact. Report the original T1 portability result (FAM:SF19) as a replication check.
design.multiplicity: One primary test: the slope of Delta on the continuous profile score. The binary-group contrast, alternative thresholds and alternative shaper definitions are secondary and corrected with Holm.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if the slope favours cut-heavy shapers (higher Delta) with a destination-clustered CI excluding 0, a permutation p below 0.01 and robustness to usage adjustment, and if the power gate passed. Rejected if the CI is entirely within a pre-set equivalence margin. Otherwise report untestable or inconclusive. Do not run the n=24 group contrast as confirmatory.
design.data_version: NBA per-game files for 2022-23 to 2025-26 (the 2025-26 regular season complete from 2026-04-13, the 2025-26 playoffs complete from 2026-06-21), as available on 2026-08-08. The derived play-type possession graph is frozen by hash before analysis, and the mover list and profile thresholds are frozen in the prereg.

methodological_questions: How is role transferability or 'traveling' measured when a player changes team?
Is n=24 units sufficient to compare cut-heavy and drive-heavy shaper groups?
How are shaper types defined from derived play-type possession records without outcome-derived labels?
How to handle role stability, regression to the mean and selection of movers, and confounding by new team context?
args.query: Do cut-heavy shapers' structural roles persist across team changes better than drive-heavy shapers' roles? Prior studies of role portability, shaper classification, role stability across teams, and small-sample limits.

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)

- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=24

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

reasoning_details.text:
I'm weighing whether another tool call is worth it. Reading the glossary could clear up what "shaper" means, and the budget allows one call, though I could also finish now and live with the uncertainty.

I'm settling on the design now: with n=24 the comparison between cut-heavy and drive-heavy groups would be underpowered, so I'd rather use the full mover set of about 294 and treat the cut-share versus drive-share as a continuous moderator. I'm also running through the statuses of the recorded hypotheses and putting rough probabilities on how this test turns out.

I'm going with do_not_proceed for the n=24 test, since that sample is too small to answer the question. The minimum viable version is a continuous moderator test over the larger mover set, and I'll make that conditional on a gate.

reasoning_details.text:
I'm weighing whether another tool call is worth it. Reading the glossary could clear up what "shaper" means, and the budget allows one call, though I could also finish now and live with the uncertainty.

I'm settling on the design now: with n=24 the comparison between cut-heavy and drive-heavy groups would be underpowered, so I'd rather use the full mover set of about 294 and treat the cut-share versus drive-share as a continuous moderator. I'm also running through the statuses of the recorded hypotheses and putting rough probabilities on how this test turns out.

I'm going with do_not_proceed for the n=24 test, since that sample is too small to answer the question. The minimum viable version is a continuous moderator test over the larger mover set, and I'll make that conditional on a gate.
